title: Delimit sampled source energy and higher first-derivative moments
statement: For uniformly Lipschitz conservative high-frequency sine fields,heat-action center derivative energy tends to d^2/(4s^2) and perpendicular-seed energy to d(d-1)/4. A positive affine background carries an order-d^2 lower bound through a fresh covariance word. At its own raw-action scale,positive K-word averaging needs K=Omega(d) to restore O(d) Gaussian Dirichlet energy. No uniform first-derivative W1,p bound exists for p>=3;an admissible scalar C1,1-potential source gives an infinite FOURTH MOMENT OF THE FIRST derivative.
